html:
A city on the Ebrie lagoon that became the capital of the French colony of Ivory Coast in 1934, and after the opening of the Vridi Canal to the sea in 1950, the main port of the region.

The canal let ocean ships into the lagoon, and the railway linked the port to Upper Volta, now Burkina Faso. Cocoa, coffee and timber poured out. Abidjan grew from a few thousand people to several million, and under Houphouet-Boigny its skyline earned it the name of the Paris of West Africa. Yamoussoukro became the official capital in 1983, but government and business stayed in Abidjan.
sum: A city on the Ebrie lagoon that became the capital of the French colony of Ivory Coast in 1934, and after the opening of the Vridi Canal to the sea in 1950, the main port of the region.
